description: Which document may have started it on one machine, ranked from the whole member list: every file name of a directory tree (a profile, a volume, an extracted collection) or of a member list (a TSV with a path column, or a path a line) is read, wherever it lies, and each macro-capable Office document is scored on signals named one by one in its row: a macro-enabled or legacy name; in a tree, a VBA project inside (the ZIP directory or an OLE directory name; no member is opened, no macro read or run), and whether that project sits under a name that is not macro-enabled; its folder (a temporary, cache, attachment or unpack folder, a downloads folder, or outside the usual document folders); a Recent shortcut of the same name; in a tree, its name in the bytes of the profile's NTUSER.DAT (where an Office MRU keeps it) and of the antivirus logs and detection files; and a Prefetch file of the document's application. A link in a tree is not followed: it is ranked by its own name, and the run is partial (a link to a directory outside the tree also gives whole_list_read false). A document whose VBA check cannot be told is ranked, with that said in its row, and the run is partial. candidates.tsv is the ranking, every candidate a row, the highest score first; coverage.json says whether the whole list was read (whole_list_read: the recipe read the whole tree or list and, for a member list, the coverage.json beside the list says the list is complete; the record is the one in the directory where the list really lies, and it stands for the list named members.tsv there; a list its own record calls partial or failed (or complete with a limit, an error or a missing segment), one with no record, or one the record does not stand for, gives false and a partial run, and list_coverage says which) and carries the rule: to answer "cannot be determined" to a "which file" question the whole member list must have been searched. A ranking is a list of candidates, not a finding. Run on demand, on a tree or a list the seat names; it is started by no trigger.
covers: The names of every file of the tree or list, and, in a tree, three readings of bytes: a document's ZIP directory or OLE directory name for a VBA project, and the candidates' names in the profile's NTUSER.DAT and in the antivirus files. It reads and runs no macro, opens no document as a document, and does not parse the registry key, the event record or the Prefetch file's list (the Windows pack's regkv, evtx_query and prefetch_mam do): a name that occurs in a hive or a log is a lead to the record. A member list has names only, so a macro in a file named .docx, the registry and the antivirus logs are not in its ranking. Other first stages (a shortcut, a script, an installer, a disc image, a OneNote file) are not ranked.
